clinician.trajectory_summary: A 26-year-old P4G1 woman with chronic hepatitis B underwent pregnancy termination at 30 weeks 2 days for fetal growth restriction and premature rupture of membranes. Following termination, she gradually developed fever, anemia, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, and coagulation dysfunction. She was transferred to ICU on day 7 post-termination in critical condition with respiratory failure, hypothermia (34.4°C), tachycardia, hypotension requiring vasopressor support, and mechanical ventilation. Laboratory investigations at the local hospital (days 1-9) revealed the classic triad of aHUS: (1) microangiopathic hemolytic anemia confirmed by peripheral blood smear showing fragmented red blood cells with elevated transaminases (AST 27.8→465 U/L, ALT 18→410 U/L) and bilirubin (8.4→15.6 μmol/L); (2) thrombocytopenia with platelet nadir of 25×10⁹/L on day 4, recovering to 48×10⁹/L by day 9; (3) acute kidney injury with creatinine rising from 38 to 781 μmol/L (peak day 4) and BUN from 2.7 to 7.26 mmol/L. Complement pathway dysfunction was documented by decreased C3 and C4 levels on ICU day 4. Negative stool and blood cultures, negative Coombs test, and negative hepatitis B DNA ruled out infectious diarrheal HUS and autoimmune hemolytic anemia. ADAMTS13 activity testing was unavailable due to COVID-19 pandemic, but peripheral blood smear analysis confirmed schistocytes, supporting aHUS over TTP. The patient underwent 9 sessions of plasma exchange along with intermittent hemofiltration and blood transfusions. Clinical response was documented with resolution of fragmented red blood cells on bone marrow biopsy, normalization of C3/C4 and platelet levels, stabilization of hemoglobin, and improvement in renal function with urine output increasing to 1300 mL/day.
